title: Compute thermal stress field
action: Compute the Cartesian thermal stress components σ_x(x,y), σ_y(x,y), τ_xy(x,y) over the fiber cross‑section for ambient temperatures T = 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 °C using the analytical thermo‑elastic solution of Tsai et al. (1991) for a two‑material elliptical‑core fiber. Stress scales linearly with ΔT = T_room - T_soft (T_soft ≈ 870 °C). Fiber geometry: elliptical core semi‑major axis 3.0 μm, semi‑minor axis 1.5 μm; outer radius 40 μm. Material constants: Δα = 1.585×10⁻⁶ °C⁻¹, E = 7750 kg/mm², ν = 0.186.

title: Calculate stress‑modified refractive index distributions
action: For each ambient temperature, convert the stress components to principal stresses via σ₁,₂ = (σ_x+σ_y)/2 ± √[((σ_x-σ_y)/2)²+τ_xy²], apply the photoelastic model n₁ = n + C₁σ₁ + C₂σ₂, n₂ = n + C₁σ₂ + C₂σ₁, n₃ = n + C₂(σ₁+σ₂) with C₁ = -6.7×10⁻⁶ kg/mm², C₂ = -41.1×10⁻⁶ kg/mm², and the isotropic core/cladding index profile derived from Δn = 0.03. Rotate to Cartesian coordinates using the stress‑dependent transformation and take the diagonal elements n_x, n_y, n_z as 2D arrays.

title: Solve vectorial Maxwell equations for propagation constants
action: For each ambient temperature T, discretize the coupled longitudinal‑field PDEs (3)–(4) using a finite‑element or finite‑difference scheme. For wavelengths around 826 nm (e.g., 816, 826, 836 nm), perform a β‑scan: replace the homogeneous RHS with random nonzero functions, solve the forced steady‑state system for trial β, compute the norm ∫ |e_z| dx dy, and locate the sharp peaks corresponding to the x‑ and y‑polarized guided modes, yielding β_x(T,λ) and β_y(T,λ).

title: Compute B, τ and write scored CSV
action: For each temperature T (10, 20, 30, 40, 50 °C), use the β_x and β_y at λ₀ = 826 nm and nearby wavelengths to approximate dB/dλ via central differences. Compute modal birefringence B = (λ₀/(2π))(β_x - β_y) and polarization mode dispersion τ = (1/c)(B – λ₀ dB/dλ) where c is the speed of light. Write a CSV file with exactly 5 rows and columns T (°C), B (dimensionless), tau (ps/m).
description: Computed modal birefringence B and polarization mode dispersion τ at five ambient temperatures.
output_schema: CSV with header: T, B, tau. T is integer °C; B is dimensionless real number; tau is real number in ps/m.
